questions.content: A composite block is made of slabs A, B, C, D and E of different thermal conductivities (given in terms of a constant K) and sizes (given in terms of length, L) as shown in the figure. All slabs are of same width. Heat Q flows only from left to right through the blocks. Then, in steady-state

options.content: heat flow through A and E slabs are same.
heat flow through slab E is maximum.
temperature difference across slab E is smallest.
heat flow through C = heat flow through B + heat flow through D.
